currentContext.business: JSW Infrastructure develops and operates ports and terminals under long-term (typically 30-50 year) concessions, offering cargo handling, storage, logistics and value-added services across dry bulk, break bulk, liquid bulk, gases and containers on India's west and east coasts. Founded in 2004 to serve JSW Steel and other group companies, it expanded from 2019 to serve third-party customers (48% of FY2026 cargo) and is now building an integrated port-led logistics platform spanning ICDs/CFS, rail rakes and Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminals through the Navkar Corporation acquisition and rail-logistics purchases. It also manages a liquid storage terminal in Fujairah, UAE and two dry-bulk terminals under O&M agreements at Fujairah and Dibba.

Ports Business: Sugar, urea, steel products, rock phosphate, molasses, gypsum, barites, laterites, edible oil handling

currentContext.strengths: Second-largest private commercial port operator in India with 183 MTPA total operational cargo-handling capacity across 13 maritime facilities|Long-term port concessions (typically 30-50 years) with a capacity-weighted average remaining concession period of around 21 years, providing predictable long-term value|Strategically located ports/terminals near key anchor customers and industrial regions (Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana) and mineral-rich hinterlands (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha), supported by multimodal evacuation infrastructure (coastal shipping fleet, rail, road, conveyor systems)|Captive anchor demand from JSW Group companies (JSW Steel, JSW Energy, JSW Cement) combined with a growing third-party customer base (48% of FY2026 cargo volume)|Building an integrated port-led logistics ecosystem (ports + ICD/CFS + 25 rail rakes) via the Navkar Corporation acquisition and rail-logistics purchases, extending reach into the hinterland
currentContext.strategies: Future growth strategy anchored on three pillars: organic expansion, acquisitions and privatisation opportunities, and sustainability.|Expand total ports and terminals capacity to approximately 400 MTPA by 2030, more than doubling current capacity through greenfield developments, brownfield expansions and strategic growth opportunities.|Build a pan-India integrated logistics platform extending into the hinterland via Inland Container Depots (ICDs), Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminals (GCTs) and rail-rake investments.|Pursue privatisation bids and value-accretive acquisitions, benefiting from the growing adoption of the Landlord Model across India's major ports which is creating a pipeline of terminal and berth privatisation opportunities.|Diversify cargo profile away from bulk-heavy cargo towards liquid, gas and container cargo.|Expand international footprint through a greenfield port project in Oman (Ash Shiwaymiyyah), aligned with Oman's Vision 2040 economic diversification agenda.|Continue to develop simultaneously three domestic greenfield ports (Jatadhar in Odisha, Murbe in Maharashtra and Keni in Karnataka) alongside modernisation of the existing portfolio, with focus on operational excellence and disciplined, timely project delivery.|Dividend is recommended annually by the Board and declared by shareholders at the AGM, paid out of profits (FY2025-26: dividend of Rs 0.90 per equity share of face value Rs 2, recommended by the Board on 8th May 2026, subject to shareholder approval at the 20th AGM). Risk oversight relevant to capital decisions follows the COSO Enterprise Risk Management framework, monitored by a Board-level Risk Management Committee (constituted under SEBI LODR Regulation 21) that periodically reviews high-risk items, mitigation plans and emerging risks/opportunities; the Board has stated no risk is assessed as threatening the Company's existence.
currentContext.expansion: Installed cargo handling capacity grew to 183 MTPA in FY2026 (from 177 MTPA in FY2025 and 170 MTPA in FY2024), and the Company targets more than doubling this to approximately 400 MTPA by FY2030 or earlier through greenfield developments, brownfield expansions, port connectivity projects and diversification into liquid, gas and container cargo. Brownfield expansion is progressing at Dharamtar (+21 MTPA) and Jaigarh (+15 MTPA), aligned with a 5 MTPA steel capacity expansion at Dolvi. Jaigarh Port has received Environmental Clearance (November 2025) to expand from 67.7 MTPA to 80 MTPA, and a Phase-III expansion of the Dharamtar Jetty Facility at Dolvi village, Raigad is under the EIA process (initiated December 2025). Ennore Coal Terminal's capacity was increased from 9.6 MTPA to 11 MTPA during FY2026 with a longer berth draft to handle capesize vessels, and the liquid berth at JNPA was modernised to a capacity of 4.5 million tonnes, with additional liquid cargo berths LB3 and LB4 at JNPA also commissioned under a PPP concession (Project Completion Certificate received from RITES Limited during the year). The Company is India's only port operator simultaneously developing three greenfield ports: Jatadhar in Odisha (initial 30 MTPA, expandable to 52 MTPA, EC obtained for 52 MTPA, 80% pile-foundation completion and 7 million CBM of dredging done, targeted for completion by March 2027, to serve JSW Utkal Steel's integrated steel plant), Murbe in Maharashtra (initial 33 MTPA, public hearing completed, EC awaited for an overall capacity of 134 MTPA) and Keni in Karnataka (30 MTPA DBFOT port, public hearing completed, EC awaited). Internationally, the Company is developing a 27 MTPA greenfield bulk port at Dhofar, Oman (Ash Shiwaymiyyah) through a 51% stake in a Port SPV, at an estimated project cost of USD 419 million. In containers, JSW Kolkata Container Terminal Private Limited signed a DBFOT concession (September 2025) for Berths 7 and 8 at Netaji Subhas Dock, Kolkata, with a capacity of 0.45 million TEUs (6.3 MTPA); detailed engineering is in progress. A ~302 km underground slurry pipeline connecting the Nuagaon mines to Jagatsinghpur (near Jatadhar Port) is under construction, with 235 km of pipeline lowering completed during FY2026. In logistics, the Company acquired 100% of JSW Rail Infra Logistics, JSW Minerals Rail Logistics and JSW (South) Rail Logistics (25 rail rakes, GPWIS/LSFTO scheme access) for Rs 1,158 crore, effective 3 February 2026, and acquired an 86-acre brownfield rail siding at Kudathini, Ballari, Karnataka, being developed into a Multi-Modal Logistics Park (ICD + Rail Freight Terminal) at a total estimated cost of Rs 380 crore, with interim operations already commenced. Two Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminals (GCTs) are being developed at Arakkonam, Tamil Nadu (2.4 MTPA on ~29.3 acres of Railway land; commissioning acknowledged and commercial operations approved by Southern Railway during the year) and Somathane, Maharashtra. The Company separately disclosed planned segment capex of Rs 9,000 crore for the logistics business and Rs 30,000 crore for the ports business over FY2025-30.
currentContext.mdna: India remained among the world's fastest-growing major economies in FY2025-26 (real GDP estimated at 7.6%, vs 7.1% in FY2024-25) despite a volatile global macro backdrop, Middle East conflict-driven crude price spikes, a weaker rupee and US tariffs.|Growth has been broad-based, driven by rural consumption, government expenditure, resilient exports and modernisation across services and infrastructure; positive momentum is expected to continue in FY2026-27.|Rising government infrastructure investment (Union Budget capex up from Rs 2 lakh crore in FY2015 to an estimated Rs 12.2 lakh crore in FY2026-27) continues to underscore infrastructure-led growth and support demand for ports and logistics.|India has emerged as the largest recipient of private participation in infrastructure investment in South Asia (over 90% of the region's total), with the government progressively expanding private-sector involvement in port infrastructure through PPP terminals; over 50% of major port capacity remains government-owned with a substantial portion yet to be privatised, presenting an expansion opportunity.|India's steel sector is expected to grow steel consumption at a 5-6% CAGR to 240-260 million tonnes by CY2035, supporting demand from anchor customer JSW Steel and related cargo volumes.|India's cement sector capacity is expected to surpass 850 MTPA by FY2028, supported by healthy demand trends and higher capital expenditure allocation, supporting bulk cargo demand.|FY2025-26 presented a challenging operating environment (inflationary pressures, supply chain disruption, Middle East conflict impact on energy markets and shipping routes) that weighed on cargo volumes industry-wide, though the Company reported operational resilience and strategic progress despite the headwinds.|Murbe Port (Palghar, Maharashtra): all-weather greenfield deepwater multi-cargo port with initial capacity of 33 MTPA; public hearing completed and awaiting Environmental Clearance for an overall capacity of 134 MTPA.|Jatadhar Port (Jagatsinghpur, Odisha): greenfield port to be built in two phases, initial capacity 30 MTPA for raw materials with expansion potential up to 52 MTPA; environmental clearance obtained for 52 MTPA, 80% completion of pile foundation works and 7 million CBM of dredging completed; construction targeted for completion by March 2027; will primarily serve JSW Utkal Steel Limited's integrated steel plant.|Keni Port (Uttara Kannada, Karnataka): all-weather greenfield deepwater DBFOT port with capacity of 30 MTPA; public hearing completed, awaiting Environmental Clearance.|Kolkata Container Terminal (Netaji Subhas Dock, Berths 7 and 8): DBFOT concession signed with Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port Authority in September 2025 for capacity of 0.45 million TEUs (6.3 MTPA); detailed engineering in progress, interim operations expected to commence soon.|Ash Shiwaymiyyah Port, Oman (Dhofar Governorate): greenfield port with initial proposed capacity of 27 MTPA to handle industrial minerals (gypsum, limestone, dolomite); Share Subscription and Purchase Agreement entered in November 2025 with Ash Shiwaymiyyah Port Company SAOC, a Minerals Development Oman SAOC entity.|Slurry pipeline connecting Nuagaon mines to Jagatsinghpur (Jatadhar Port vicinity), approximately 302 km underground; 235 km of pipeline lowering completed during the year.

risks.note: IMF projects global growth slowing to 3.1% in CY2026 and 3.2% in CY2027 as geopolitical tensions, particularly the Middle East conflict, weigh on economic activity; the conflict has driven disruptions to commodity markets, tighter financial conditions and elevated energy prices, which can affect global trade flows and cargo volumes relevant to the Company's port business.

risks.risk: US tariff escalation and trade-policy uncertainty
risks.note: Higher US tariffs could weigh on India's exports and manufacturing activity in subsequent quarters; since export/import cargo movement is a direct driver of the Company's volumes, sustained tariff or trade-policy shocks are a demand risk.

risks.risk: Anchor-customer / related-party concentration with the JSW Group
risks.note: Material related-party transactions during the year were between wholly-owned subsidiaries JSW Jaigarh Port Limited and JSW Dharamtar Port Private Limited with JSW Steel Limited, and JSW Port Logistics Private Limited with JSW Shipping & Logistics Private Limited, indicating continued dependence on JSW Group cargo and captive/group-company relationships even as third-party cargo share grows.

risks.risk: Compliance, operational and strategic risk under the Company's own ERM framework
risks.note: The Company's Enterprise Risk Management Framework explicitly acknowledges that compliance-related, operational and strategic risks can disrupt operations and affect the achievement of its objectives, requiring continuous risk identification, assessment and mitigation across a large multi-site port and logistics network.

risks.risk: Energy price and input-cost volatility linked to the West Asia conflict
risks.note: RBI projects that persistently elevated energy prices due to the West Asia conflict, along with possible El Nino conditions, could pose upside risks to inflation — a cost pressure relevant to the fuel- and power-intensive nature of port and cargo-handling operations.

risks.risk: Health, safety and environment risk inherent to cargo-handling operations
risks.note: As a cargo handling and maritime logistics operator, the Company targets a 'Zero Harm' environment and has invested in a Safety Experience Centre, AI-enabled monitoring and Permit-to-Work systems, indicating that workplace/operational safety across ports, terminals and last-mile logistics remains a material risk area requiring continuous management attention.

one-line thesis: JSW Infrastructure Ltd, a leading port infrastructure company, has received a credit rating of CARE AA with a stable outlook for its subsidiary Paradip East Quay Coal Terminal Private Limited, indicating a strong financial position and stable cash flows. The company's focus on sustainable infrastructure and logistics is expected to drive growth. With a strong parent company and a well-performing subsidiary, JSW Infrastructure Ltd is well-positioned for future expansion.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
